scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: At [01:14]-[01:56], when the customer expressed anxiety about his newborn baby and the heating cutting out during a cold snap, the agent failed to offer any empathy or acknowledgment and jumped coldly into technical specifications.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: At [09:13], the agent asked what brand of smart thermostat the customer was trying to pair, even though the customer had already stated at [01:41] that it was a Hive Mini.

scorecard.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
scorecard.coaching: At [06:07], the agent made a condescending remark blaming the customer for not reading the manual ('Well, if you'd actually read the quick-start booklet that came in the box, you'd know IoT devices need a dedicated 2.4 gigahertz SSID').

grader.scenario: Wi-Fi 6 router band-steering preventing 2.4GHz smart heating thermostat and baby monitor from staying connected
grader.notes: Hard-case E, AL, R FAILs paired with strong technical O, PR, H, RE PASSes under STT roughness. Agent Hannah never acknowledges Oluwaseun's anxiety about his newborn baby in a cold house ([01:14]-[01:56]), makes a condescending remark about reading the quick-start booklet at [06:07], and re-asks the thermostat brand at [09:13] after he named the Hive Mini at [01:41]. However, she takes complete technical ownership ([06:51]-[11:39]), manages a 52s hold properly ([07:50]-[08:52]), and confirms live resolution ([14:07]).

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: [00:00] Agent opens with 'thank you for calling S-Net' and [14:33] closes with 'thank you for choosing S-Net'.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: [07:50] Agent announces the hold ('please bear with me while i apply the split SSID settings') before the 52s gap and [08:52] thanks the customer on return ('thank you for holding oluwaseun').

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: [00:24]-[00:46] Agent verifies postcode, home address, four-digit security PIN, and security question within the first minute of the call.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: [00:24], [08:52], and [13:56] Agent addresses the customer by his first name, Oluwaseun.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [01:14] Customer says 'we have a six day old newborn baby in the house and there is a freezing cold snap outside right now' and [01:41] 'it's honestly making my wife and me so anxious', and [01:30]/[01:56] Agent responds with zero empathy or acknowledgment.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [01:56] Agent restates the problem in her own words: 'your S-Net Wi-Fi 6 hub is using automatic band steering on a single combined network name which is knocking your 2.4 gigahertz heating receiver and baby camera offline'.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [01:41] Customer states 'the thermostat is a Hive Mini', but at [09:13] Agent asks 'And what brand of smart thermostat are you trying to pair to the network?'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [06:51]-[09:53] Agent takes full technical ownership by remotely splitting the 2.4GHz and 5GHz radios via TR-069, disabling PMF, locking channel 6, and [11:39] setting static DHCP IP reservations.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [06:07] Agent says condescendingly: 'Well, if you'd actually read the quick-start booklet that came in the box, you'd know IoT devices need a dedicated 2.4 gigahertz SSID.'

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: [02:26]-[05:01] Agent probes into device distance from the hub, app error messages, WPA2/WPA3 security mode, third-party mesh extenders, hardware revision, and power supply setup.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [10:24], [11:27], and [14:07] Customer connects both the Owlet baby monitor and Hive Mini thermostat live on the call, hears the boiler fire up, and confirms both show solid green/blue status lights.
